title: Learned catalyst search guides oxygen-evolution catalysts made from meteorites
summary: A robotic chemistry system combined a neural-network performance model with theoretical calculations and experimental calibration to select a catalyst formulation from five Martian meteorite feedstocks. Laboratory testing of the selected formulation measured an oxygen-evolution overpotential of 445.1 mV at 10 mA per square centimetre, lower than the compared theory-only and experiment-only search formulations. The work demonstrates a terrestrial laboratory catalyst result; oxygen production on Mars and a globally optimal composition were not independently established.
ai_technology: Neural-network oxygen-evolution performance prediction; model-guided composition search
organization: University of Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: The primary journal supplement compares measured overpotentials of 445.1 mV for the combined model-guided formulation, 467.4 mV for experiment-guided optimization and 542.7 mV for theory-guided selection. The original preprint abstract already reports the 445.1 mV result and more than 550000 seconds of operation.
evidence.unknown: The first located preprint was posted March 23, 2023; the journal version appeared November 13, 2023, with a March 2024 issue date. The preprint body was inaccessible; version-specific result presence is established from its primary deposited abstract, while detailed comparator measurements come from the journal supplement. Search-space coverage does not prove global optimality. Mars deployment, resource extraction at scale and integrated life-support performance remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: A learned neural-network model combines first-principles and robot-generated experimental information to predict oxygen-evolution performance and guide which mixed-meteorite catalyst formulation to synthesize and test.

source_review.scope: Primary preprint metadata and deposited abstract; journal front/abstract/code-availability and full author supplement, including model-guided experimental comparison. Main journal body and preprint body were not read.
